quotes.basis: Project site lists '3.5 BHK 2125 Sq.Ft => Rs 3.15 Cr* Onwards' (3.15Cr/2125sqft=Rs14,824/sqft) and '4.5 BHK 3000 Sq.Ft => Rs 4.49 Cr* Onwards' (4.49Cr/3000sqft=Rs14,967/sqft)

quotes.basis: Developer page states 'Price starting @ 4.25 Cr.' for 3BHK/4BHK units sized 2375-3295 sq ft super built-up (220.64-306.11 sq mtrs); computed from stated starting price and stated minimum super-built-up area: 4.25Cr / 2375 sqft = Rs17,895/sqft. Per-sqft figure itself not stated by developer, only starting total price + size range.

Press article (project-listicle) states 'current pricing starting at Rs 4.25 crore' with 'RERA carpet area falls within the range of 1,288 to 1,786 sq ft' for 3 BHK / 3 BHK+Study / 4 BHK homes. This corroborates the Rs4.25Cr starting price from the developer's own site, but on RERA CARPET area (1,288 sqft min) rather than the super-built-up area (2375 sqft) the developer site quotes -- carpet-area psf would compute far higher (~Rs33,000/sqft) than the super-built-up psf used in the other quote row (Rs17,895/sqft). Not treated as a distinct psf figure here since the area basis is ambiguous/inconsistent between the two sources; flagged for the sanity-check pass instead.
quotes.snippet: It has 3 BHK, 3 BHK + Study and 4 BHK homes and the RERA carpet area falls within the range of 1,288 to 1,786 sq ft with current pricing starting at Rs4.25 crore.

quotes.basis: Developer site states 'Starting from ₹1.6 Cr* Onwards'; smallest listed configuration is 2.5 BHK, 1,300-1,500 sq ft (individual config price shown as 'Coming Soon', so exact per-config price not separately published) => ₹1.6 Cr / 1,300-1,500 sq ft = ₹10,667-12,308/sq ft, applying the stated starting price to the smallest config

sector_news.headline: Dwarka E-way area sees 135% rise in home prices in 5 years: Report
sector_news.figure: ANAROCK data: avg residential prices on Dwarka Expressway rose from Rs6,032/sqft (2021) to Rs14,180/sqft (H1 2026), vs Gurugram citywide avg of Rs13,350/sqft; homes above Rs2.5cr now a prominent budget segment; >Rs2.2 lakh crore infra capital deployed around the corridor

sector_news.headline: Dwarka Expressway challenges Gurugram's old luxury addresses after 135% price surge
sector_news.figure: ANAROCK data (same week as the HT 135% report, but a notably higher figure): avg residential prices in the Dwarka Expressway micro-market now ~Rs21,700-24,000/sqft; homes priced above Rs2.5cr are the dominant new-supply budget segment; 3-BHK units are 39% of new supply. NOTE: this Rs21,700-24,000/sqft figure and HT's Rs14,180/sqft figure are both attributed to ANAROCK for the same corridor in the same week -- a real discrepancy in press reporting, not a typo on our part (possibly blended-average vs new-launch-only cuts of the same dataset).

sector_news.headline: Dwarka Expressway property prices double in 7 years: How infrastructure turned NCR corridor into a wealth creator
sector_news.figure: ANAROCK data: avg Dwarka Expressway price rose from Rs5,359/sqft (2019) to over Rs9,600/sqft (H1 2024); industry estimates put cumulative appreciation at 95-105% since 2019, accelerating to 110-120% between 2021 and early 2026. Example cited: Hero Homes (Sector 104) launched Nov 2018 at ~Rs5,000/sqft, now ~Rs16,500/sqft (+230% since launch).

sector_news.headline: Move over Bengaluru and Hyderabad: Noida and Gurugram top property price appreciation with up to 125% growth
sector_news.figure: ANAROCK data: Gurugram citywide avg residential price rose from Rs6,150/sqft (2019) to Rs13,350/sqft (Q2 2026), +117% (this is a citywide figure, not corridor/sector-specific; Noida's comparable rise was +125%, Mumbai +64% to Rs29,270/sqft)
